name: KS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Mann's large fundraising advantage ($2.7M cash vs. under $5K)
Incumbent seeking re-election with no polling or ratings suggesting vulnerability
Libertarian on ballot may siphon minor votes
model.rationale: The district's R+16 lean, Mann's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial edge leave Reinhold with no visible path; markets price her win chance near 4%. No polls or expert ratings indicate any reason to move materially from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or a major late outside-spending intervention against Mann would be the only realistic route to a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kansas's 1st District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+16. Tracey Mann, the incumbent, is running for re-election and holds a commanding financial position: he has raised nearly $1.5 million and sits on $2.7 million cash on hand, while Democrat Lauren Reinhold has raised under $50,000 with minimal reserves. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Mann roughly a 95% chance of winning. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
